findings.rationale: Local performance at round 20 shows observed prevalence (0.211) well above the model's mean prediction (0.142), giving CITL -0.069 (z -4.6) and ECE z +4.9, while AUC (0.827) is normal, which is the prevalence_shift signature rather than label noise. The Sex subgroup O/E ratio for group 1.0 is 1.59 (z_noise 6.3), so the excess positives are not confined to one group. Its update norm ratio climbs steadily from about 1.1 in rounds 1-3 to 1.88 at round 6 and about 3.5 by round 20, with cosine turning negative from about round 8. Drift tests show no feature drift, so the anomaly is in the outcome, not the features. Onset is estimated at round 6 from the rising norm; the exact onset is uncertain.

Local performance at round 20 shows observed prevalence (0.210) well above mean prediction (0.142), giving CITL -0.069 (z -4.4) and ECE z +4.0, with normal AUC (0.801). The Sex group 1.0 O/E ratio is 1.41 (z_noise 4.3). Update norms rise from about 0.7-1.0 in rounds 1-5 to 1.42 at round 6 and about 2.3-2.6 later, with mostly negative cosine from round 6. This pattern matches a client whose outcome labels are systematically higher than its features imply. The evidence is somewhat weaker than for NY because the client is smaller.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then spent the remaining budget confirming leads with per-round views for NY, CA, VI and client_updates for NY and CA. Two clients, NY and CA, show a consistent multi-tool signature: CITL around -0.07 with observed prevalence about 0.21 against a predicted 0.14, normal AUC, elevated Sex-subgroup O/E, and update norms that grow over rounds with negative cosine. I read this as prevalence_shift rather than label_noise (AUC is normal) or poisoning (local performance is anomalous too). NY is the stronger case. Weaker leads were not reported: GU (small client, Sex shift and CITL at about 3 z), VI (erratic per-round drift that looks like noise), and WV/SD/IL/DC feature-level outliers (single noise-dominated values). Feature-level noise is large for small clients, so I did not treat those as missing-artefact evidence. No sign of free-riding, sign-flip poisoning, or subgroup under-diagnosis was found.
